small_guidance:
- The fused conv kernel uses `[OC, TW]` accumulator with TW=16 and OC=16 — try larger TW (32 or 64) to amortize weight loads, sweep `num_warps` ∈ {4, 8} and `num_stages` ∈ {2, 3, 4} via `triton.autotune`.
- In `softmax_maxpool_kernel`, BLOCK_C=16 with `num_warps=2` is tiny; try one program per `(n, do, ho)` row processing all `Wo` outputs to amortize the 64 strided loads, or bump `num_warps=4` and tile multiple pool windows per program.
- Consider laying out `conv` as channels_last (N, OD, OH, OW, OC) so the softmax+pool kernel reads OC contiguously per spatial point — currently OC stride is `OD*OH*OW` causing strided gathers.
large_guidance:
- Fuse conv + softmax + 4×4×4 maxpool in a single kernel (skip the intermediate `conv` tensor): one program per `(n, do, ho, wo)` computes all 64 conv outputs for the 4³ window across all OC=16 channels into a `[OC, 64]` register tile, applies per-position softmax along OC, then reduces max along the 64 axis. Total FLOPs per program: 64 positions × 16 OC × 3 IC × 27 = ~83K, fits easily; this eliminates the OD*OH*OW intermediate write/read entirely.
- Use im2col-style GEMM: load the 6×6×6 input patch per IC into shared/registers once, then do `[OC, 64] = [OC, IC*27] @ [IC*27, 64]` via `tl.dot`, exploiting tensor cores. Weight `[OC=16, IC*27=81]` is tiny and fits in registers; reuse across all 64 spatial outputs of the pool window.
- Switch input/weight to channels-last so the IC dimension is the contiguous GEMM-K axis, enabling vectorized loads and `tl.dot` accumulation.
